contrary_evidence: The latest COFER quarter shows the dollar share rising to 57.13%, partly because of FX valuation, which argues against an abrupt break from the dollar reserve system.
Central-bank gold purchases were only 57 tonnes in revised Q1 2026 before rebounding to 289 tonnes in Q2, rejecting a smooth continuously accelerating diversification path.
UNCTAD notes that the 2025 FDI rebound was narrow and concentrated; announced greenfield projects do not guarantee realized productive investment.
Rare-earth refining concentration declined modestly between 2023 and 2025, providing a counterexample to a universal increase in processing concentration.
limitations: The monitor combines datasets with different frequencies and publication lags; it therefore cannot establish a literal weekly global capital-flow total.
World Gold Council official-sector demand is an estimate because no single official source provides timely complete global physical central-bank purchases.
TIC geographic attribution is affected by custodians and financial centres and should not be read as ultimate beneficial ownership.
Several productive-investment conclusions rely on announced greenfield project values and forward electricity forecasts rather than completed capital expenditure.
The EIA September 2026 outlook is forecast-based and depends on assumptions about Middle East export constraints and oil-market normalization.
notes: Approved as a bilingual weekly monitor. Central quantitative claims were corroborated and the report explicitly avoids invalid aggregation of financial positions, reserves, resource values and physical infrastructure. Confidence remains medium because several structural series are lagged or estimated and some forward-looking energy/infrastructure conclusions depend on forecasts and announced projects.
